blocks.etymology: From Middle English thorny, þorny, þorni, from Old English þorniġ, from Proto-West Germanic *þornag. By surface analysis, thorn + -y.

senses.definition: Causing a lot of problems, arguments, or difficulty to deal with.

examples.en: Tax reform has always been a thorny political issue.
examples.vi: Cải cách thuế luôn là một vấn đề chính trị gai góc.

examples.en: The committee tried to avoid that thorny topic during the meeting.
examples.vi: Ủy ban đã cố gắng tránh chủ đề hắc búa đó trong cuộc họp.

senses.vi: gai góc; hắc búa; phức tạp

senses.definition: Having sharp points on the stems or leaves.

examples.en: Be careful when walking near those thorny rose bushes.
examples.vi: Hãy cẩn thận khi đi gần những bụi hoa hồng nhiều gai đó.

thesaurus.definition: having or covered with protective barbs or quills or spines or thorns or setae etc.

vi_block: Gai góc, khó khăn, hắc búa.

wiktionary.gloss: Having thorns or spines.

examples: thorny issues
wiktionary.gloss: Troublesome or vexatious.
Aloof and irritable.

blocks.etymology: From tree + bark.

blocks.etymology: From Latin ultimatus (“late, last final”), from Latin ultimus (“extreme, last, furthest, farthest, final”).

senses.definition: a final demand that threatens serious action if not accepted in time.

examples.en: The manager gave him an ultimatum: arrive on time or get fired.
examples.vi: Người quản lý đã đưa ra tối hậu thư cho anh: đến đúng giờ hoặc bị đuổi việc.

thesaurus.definition: a final peremptory demand

vi_block: Nguyên tắc cơ bản, nguyên lý cơ bản.

wiktionary.gloss: A final statement of terms or conditions made by one party to another, especially one that expresses a threat of reprisal or war if the terms are not met before some specified date and time.
An intended final statement of terms or conditions made by one party to another in a negotiation.

blocks.etymology: From Arabic وَصْلَةٌ (waṣlatun).

wiktionary.gloss: A diacritic added to the Arabic letter alif ا to form ٱ, also called "hamzatu l-waṣli" - هَمْزَةُ الْوَصْلِ (hamzatu l-waṣli) or "alifu l-waṣli" - أَلِفُ الْوَصْلِ (ʔalifu l-waṣli). It denotes elision and is seldom used in practice in fully vocalised Arabic texts, only to highlight that the alif is silent هَمْزَةُ ٱلْوَصْلِ (hamzatu l-waṣli) = هَمْزَةُ الْوَصْلِ (hamzatu l-waṣli).

blocks.etymology: From Middle English yelpynge, from Old English ġilping; equivalent to yelp + -ing.

the frenzied yelpings of the huntsman's dogs
